title: Chapter 52: First Date
html:
Several deep breaths and a splash of cold water finally steadied Chen Ge’s nerves.

“It’s time to go.”

He retrieved the backpack from his previous mission and packed Zhang Ya’s love letter, a power bank, and a mallet. Having learned from last time, he slipped the penknife into his trouser pocket and tucked the doll his parents had left him into his shirt pocket. His clothes bulged in several places, but at least he felt safer.

Once he had everything, he locked the Haunted House and hurried out of New Century Park. It was already 12:15 a.m., and the roads were nearly empty. Another ten minutes passed before he managed to hail a cab.

“Western Jiujiang’s Private Academy, please. I’m in a hurry, so step on it if you can.”

“No problem, get in.”

The driver was an easygoing middle-aged man with a fondness for nineties pop. Chen Ge used the ride to research his mission from the back seat.

The first thing the black phone had mentioned was Andersen’s The Red Shoes, so he began there. He found the original fairy tale online, skimmed it, and immediately regretted doing so.

Its plot differed little from the black phone’s version. A young girl received a beautiful pair of red dancing shoes and loved them so much that she wore them everywhere—even to church, where she was cursed to dance without end. Terrified and exhausted, she finally begged an executioner to chop off her feet. The tale’s strangest turn came afterward: still wearing the shoes, the severed feet danced away into the forest.

Is this even a fairy tale?

That did nothing to calm him. His mission, after all, was to find Zhang Ya’s red dancing shoes.

When I received the cursed love letter, the black phone gave me a brief description of Zhang Ya. She died in a bloodstained school uniform and red dancing shoes. Could the fairy tale be literal? Once she put the shoes on, was she unable to remove them?

His skin crawled. This mission was unlike any before it. He would be confronting a Red Specter—one whose hatred ran deep enough to generate a Bloody Heart Mission.

Looks like the key to tonight’s mission is the red dancing shoes.

He reread the story several times. Its obvious moral was a warning against vanity and a lesson in humility.

But why did the black phone invoke this story at the beginning of the mission?

Unable to find an answer, he turned his attention to Western Jiujiang’s Private Academy. The school had operated for only two years before closing and had stood abandoned ever since. Online explanations ranged from budget problems to prohibitively high tuition.

He combed through the results, but Zhang Ya’s name never appeared. According to the internet, she had never been connected to the school at all.

There has to be something more sinister about the closure than what’s been speculated online!

Beyond the window, streetlights streamed backward through the darkness. Chen Ge narrowed his eyes in thought. What kind of death turns a girl into a Red Specter? Why does she carry so much hatred? And what do the red dancing shoes have to do with it?

Lost in thought, he barely noticed the radio grow louder. He looked up to find the driver watching him through the rearview mirror.

“What’s troubling you, young man? You look miserable.” The driver was a born chatterbox. He had tried to start a conversation as soon as Chen Ge got in, but Chen Ge had been too absorbed in his research to respond.

“My life has changed a lot recently, and I’m still trying to make sense of it. I suppose I’m feeling overwhelmed.” Chen Ge put away his phone and offered a polite smile.

“Take it one step at a time. Things will work themselves out. When I get stressed, I put on some disco and shake it off. You’d be amazed how much better you feel.” The driver bounced to the beat.

At least the man is optimistic,thought Chen Ge.

“By the way, why are you going to the Private Academy so late at night? That place is mostly abandoned, and it’s not close to any residential area.”

Chen Ge opened his mouth, hesitated, then answered, “I’m going on a date.”

“A date? At this ungodly hour?” The driver glanced back at Chen Ge.

“It’s true. She’s a little difficult to please, and she has some unusual tastes.” Chen Ge tried to make the situation sound normal. No girl had ever asked him on a date before; despite the circumstances, the invitation still gave his ego a small boost.

“That’s wonderful! What are you worried about—her not liking you? Though I have to ask, who dresses like that for a date? Men need to make an effort these days too. That backpack clashes with everything else you’re wearing.”

The driver’s floodgates opened, leaving Chen Ge no chance to reply. Anyone else would have been thrilled about a first date. His felt more like coercion mixed with a desperate attempt to stay alive.

“Don’t come on too strong. Skip boring topics like the weather, pay her a compliment, and listen when she speaks. First impressions matter…” As the advice continued, Chen Ge considered playing Wedding Dress on his phone so they could both enjoy some peace and quiet.

The taxi sped into the night. Traffic thinned, then the buildings did too. Even the streetlights began to vanish as the last signs of civilization fell behind them and the forest swallowed the road.

The driver glanced at the GPS and asked Chen Ge, “Are you sure you got the right address? Other than an abandoned school, there’s nothing down the road.”

“I’m sure. Just drop me near the school. How much do I owe you?”

“Nineteen. Would you mind paying by WeChat? I just started my shift and don’t have change.”

“No problem.”

When Chen Ge pulled out his phone, the penknife came with it and landed on the seat. The driver spotted the blade and leaned subtly away. Reaching to lower the radio, he used his little finger to press a button on the console.

Chen Ge saw everything. All he could do was keep smiling. The driver had clearly mistaken him for a burglar prowling the outskirts after midnight.

“Payment sent.” Chen Ge pocketed his phone and glanced toward the driver’s seat. “Uncle, are you recording this for the police?”

The driver was taking a drink of water. He broke into a violent coughing fit and waved both hands in denial.

“I understand why, but…” Chen Ge turned toward the school’s eerie silhouette in the darkness.

“…I’m really here for a date.”
